name: @vispero/cora-mcp

tools.name: scan_page
tools.description: Checks the page the browser shows now with the accessibility rules the project's config runs on it, or only those the `rules` selectors name, as the agent left it after navigating, clicking, typing or running script, such as with a dialog open. Scans the current tab, or the tab at `tab`. Returns the issues found, most severe first, each with an ID that explain_finding and verify_fix take, its fix class and, on an app built with CORA's source stamps, its source location and how many call sites it has; an issue whose rule the project's config sets to `report` has `report: true`, and never fails CI's gate. Says when the page did not settle before the scan, so another scan of it can find other issues. Records the run in the project's state directory, in runs/ (.cora/runs/ by default), and each issue's element as the scan found it in its loop/, for verify_fix. Its issues never fail a gate or change a baseline, since no one can reach the page state again on demand, so none is marked as one the project's baseline accepts; to check a page as it loads, use scan_url. Automated rules find only some accessibility problems: a scan that finds none does not show the page is accessible.

tab.description: The index of the tab to scan, as browser_tabs lists it; the current tab when absent.

include.description: CSS selectors in the main document: scan only these elements and their content. A scoped scan records partial coverage. One that matches an element on or inside one the config's page.exclude leaves out fails with scan.invalid-scope.

exclude.description: CSS selectors in the main document: leave these elements and their content out of the scan. A scoped scan records partial coverage. The config's page.exclude for the page applies beside them.

rules.description: Rule selectors: run only the rules these name, of those the project's config runs on the page, each a rule ID such as axe/region, a WCAG success criterion such as 1.4.3, a category such as forms, or an engine's rules such as axe/*. A narrowed scan never runs a rule the config leaves off, and records a run of its own.

tools.name: scan_url
tools.description: Loads a URL in the current tab, as cora scan loads a target, and checks the page as it loads with the accessibility rules the project's config runs on it, or only those the `rules` selectors name. A load that fails or answers an HTTP error, a page that keeps navigating or stops answering while it is scanned, and a scan that runs out of time are reported as not scanned, and so is a redirect to another page, such as a sign-in page, whose landing page is scanned in its place when it is on the same host. Returns the issues found, most severe first, each with an ID that explain_finding and verify_fix take, its fix class and, on an app built with CORA's source stamps, its source location and how many call sites it has; an issue whose rule the project's config sets to `report` has `report: true`, and never fails CI's gate. Says when the page did not settle before the scan, so another scan of it can find other issues. Records the run in the project's state directory, in runs/ (.cora/runs/ by default), and each issue's element as the scan found it in its loop/, for verify_fix. An issue the project's baseline accepts, as cora scan counts it, has `accepted: true`, so CI's gate does not fail on it. Automated rules find only some accessibility problems: a scan that finds none does not show the page is accessible.

url.description: The page to load: an absolute http or https URL, or a path resolved against the config's baseUrl.

include.description: CSS selectors in the main document: scan only these elements and their content. A scoped scan records partial coverage. One that matches an element on or inside one the config's page.exclude leaves out fails with scan.invalid-scope.

exclude.description: CSS selectors in the main document: leave these elements and their content out of the scan. A scoped scan records partial coverage. The config's page.exclude for the page applies beside them.

rules.description: Rule selectors: run only the rules these name, of those the project's config runs on the page, each a rule ID such as axe/region, a WCAG success criterion such as 1.4.3, a category such as forms, or an engine's rules such as axe/*. A narrowed scan never runs a rule the config leaves off, and records a run of its own.

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: Lists the accessibility rules scan_page and scan_url run for this project by its config's rule selection: on the page at `url` when given, as its route's selection decides them, and otherwise where no route of the config sets its own; with `rules` selectors, such as `forms` or `axe/*`, only those they name. Each rule gives its ID, what it checks, its WCAG success criteria, its category, whether its findings fail the gate (`on`) or are only reported (`report`), `decidedBy`, the config's key that decided it, such as `rules.standard` or `routes[0].rules.overrides["axe/region"]`, and the severity and fix class of the issues it finds.

url.description: The page whose rules to list, as scan_url takes it: an absolute http or https URL, or a path resolved against the config's baseUrl. Its route's rule selection decides the rules; without it, the config's rules where no route sets its own.

rules.description: Rule selectors: list only the rules these name, each a rule ID such as axe/region, a WCAG success criterion such as 1.4.3, a category such as forms, or an engine's rules such as axe/*.

tools.name: explain_finding
tools.description: Explains an issue from a scan's result: its rule, WCAG success criteria and fix class, `report: true` when the project's config sets its rule to `report`, so it never fails CI's gate, `accepted: true` when the project's baseline accepts it in the run, as cora scan counts it, so CI's gate does not fail on it, how many call sites it has, the combinations of browser and viewport its findings were seen in, and each of its findings with its page, element, source location, markup and why it failed. Each finding's `reproduce` names its page, its `url` in its `browser` and `viewport`, and how to reach it again, setting its viewport with browser_resize, by its `kind`: `load`, rescan its `url` with scan_url; `state`, reach its named `state` again, as the test that named it does, then rescan with scan_page; `none`, open its `url` and repeat the interaction that reached the page, then rescan with scan_page. Its `verify` names the rule the rescan must run and the issue ID to look for in the rescan's result. Without `run`, the newest run that holds the issue in the project's state directory, in runs/ (.cora/runs/ by default), is read, so an issue from a cora scan run can be explained too.

issue.description: The issue's ID, as a scan's result lists it.

run.description: The run that holds the issue, as a scan's result names it; the newest run that holds it when absent.

tools.name: get_fix_guidance
tools.description: Gives how to fix a rule's failures in any framework: the rule in plain language, who its failures affect, and each situation the rule fails in with its fix, in Markdown, and, where it helps, the markup after the fix, in HTML. Also lists the fixes that silence the rule or look right but still fail people, and why. Takes the rule ID that list_rules, scan_page, scan_url and explain_finding give. With the project's `framework`, such as react, its `framework` adds the rule's fixes in that framework's syntax where they differ from those for any framework; it is absent where they do not. Its `docsUrl` is the rule's guidance page on CORA's docs site, to show a person.

rule.description: The rule's ID, as list_rules or a scan's result gives it, such as axe/image-alt.

framework.description: The project's UI framework, whose fixes the result adds in its syntax where they differ; without it, the result gives the guidance for any framework alone.

tools.name: verify_fix
tools.description: Checks a fix of an issue that scan_page or scan_url found, by its ID, and records the attempt. Rescans the issue's page in the browser and viewport it was found in: a page reached by navigation is loaded again at its URL in the current tab, and a page reached by interaction is scanned as the current tab shows it, so reach that page state again first. Set the viewport with browser_resize first when the tab's differs. Finds the element by the selector the scan recorded or, on an app built with CORA's source stamps, by where its opening tag starts in the source, so a fix that changes its class, or turns a div into a button, is still checked. Compares the element's accessibility-tree entry when the issue was found with its entry now, and returns the verdict: `fixed`; `still-failing`, with `listedAs`, the ID the rescan lists the issue under, which an edit to the element can change; `suppressed` when the fix hid the element from assistive technology, such as with aria-hidden, display: none or an empty alt, rather than fixing it; or `inconclusive`, with its `reason`, when the rescan did not cover the rule there, the evidence is missing, or the element cannot be found, as when the fix moved its tag to other lines or the tag renders several elements. `report: true` says the project's config sets the issue's rule to `report` on its page, so the issue never fails CI's gate. With `still-failing`, `accepted: true` says the project's baseline accepts the issue as the rescan lists it, so CI's gate does not fail on it. Its `next` says what to do: `continue` fixing the issue, `done`, or `escalate` it to a person once 3 attempts have not fixed it. Records the rescan in the project's state directory, in runs/ (.cora/runs/ by default). It carries `unsettled` when the rescan's page did not settle before it was scanned, so the verdict may judge a page still changing: act on the verdict, and treat the page as unsettled, as a scan's. A `fixed` verdict means the rule no longer finds the issue, not that the element is accessible.

issue.description: The issue's ID, as a scan's result lists it.

tools.name: summarize_fixes
tools.description: Reports what became of each issue whose remediation loop is open, every issue a scan found whether or not a fix was tried, from the loop records in the project's state directory, in loop/ (.cora/loop/ by default), and ends each loop it reports: call it last, once each fix is verified with verify_fix. Pass in `fixes` an entry for each issue you changed, proposed a change for or left for a person: its ID, your account of it, and the test that pins the fix when one does. Each issue gives its rule in plain language, who it affects, its WCAG success criteria or, for a best practice, that it is not a WCAG failure, `report: true` when the project's config sets its rule to `report`, so it never fails CI's gate, `accepted: true` when the project's baseline accepted it in the latest scan that compared it with the baseline, as cora scan counts it, so CI's gate does not fail on it, its page and element, the issue's severity, each place in the source its findings sit at and its call sites as the scan found them, your account and the test, the element's accessibility-tree entry before and after the last fix, and links to each criterion's Understanding page, the rule's documentation and its guidance page. Its `disposition` is `fixed` when verify_fix last found it fixed, `escalated` when its loop escalated it to a person, and otherwise `proposed`, for a person to review the fix you propose or make the one that needs their judgement. An issue left out, for the size of the result or while a verification of it runs, keeps its loop, and `omitted` counts them: call again for the rest, passing their entries.

fixes.description: An entry for each issue you changed, proposed a change for or left for a person, by any ID it has had: your account of it, and the test that pins the fix when one does.

issue.description: The issue's ID, as a scan's result lists it.

change.description: Your account of the issue for a person to review. The summary cuts it past 2048 characters of its JSON text, where each double quote, backslash, tab or line break takes two, as does each emoji, so markup with quoted attributes is cut sooner: keep it well within that. For an issue you fixed or that escalated, what you changed or tried, with no marker. Otherwise it starts with a marker: "Applied as decided:" for a person's decision you applied but could not verify, "Proposed:" for the exact change a person should make or approve, or "Not changed:" for what a person must check or decide.

test.description: The test that pins the fix, by its file and name, such as tests/forms.spec.ts › 'the phone field has a name'.

tools.description: Handle a dialog

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

function.description: () => { /* code */ } or (element) => { /* code */ } when element is provided

filename.description: File name to save the result to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not provided, result is returned as text.

tools.name: browser_file_upload
tools.description: Upload one or multiple files

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

annotations.title: Drop files or data onto an element

tools.name: browser_find
tools.description: Search the accessibility snapshot of the current page for text or a regular expression. Returns matching snapshot nodes with a few lines of surrounding context (like search snippets), each shown under its path from the root of the tree, which is cheaper than capturing the whole snapshot when you only need to locate an element and its ref.

text.description: Plain text to search for in the page snapshot (case-insensitive substring match). Provide either text or regex, not both.

regex.description: Regular expression to search for in the page snapshot. Matching is case-sensitive by default; wrap the pattern in slashes to add flags, e.g. "/error/i" for case-insensitive. Provide either text or regex, not both.

filename.description: Save results to a file instead of returning them in the response. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root.

tools.name: browser_fill_form
tools.description: Fill multiple form fields

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

value.description: Value to fill in the field. If the field is a checkbox, the value should be `true` or `false`. If the field is a combobox, the value should be the text of the option.

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description: Press a key on the keyboard

key.description: Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type text into editable element

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

text.description: Text to type into the element

submit.description: Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)

slowly.description: Whether to type one character at a time. Useful for triggering key handlers in the page. By default entire text is filled in at once.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL

tools.name: browser_navigate_back
tools.description: Go back to the previous page in the history

tools.name: browser_network_requests
tools.description: Returns a numbered list of network requests since loading the page. Use browser_network_request with the number to get full details.

static.description: Whether to include successful static resources like images, fonts, scripts, etc. Defaults to false.

filter.description: Only return requests whose URL matches this regexp (e.g. "/api/.*user").

filename.description: File name to save the network requests to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not provided, requests are returned as text.

tools.name: browser_network_request
tools.description: Returns full details (headers and body) of a single network request, or a single part if `part` is set. Use the number from browser_network_requests.

index.description: 1-based index of the request, as printed by browser_network_requests.

part.description: Return only this part of the request. Omit to return full details.

filename.description: File name to save the result to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not provided, output is returned as text.

tools.name: browser_take_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. You can't perform actions based on the screenshot, use browser_snapshot for actions.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

type.description: Image format for the screenshot. If unset, inferred from the filename extension, otherwise png.

filename.description: File name to save the screenshot to. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root. If not specified, the screenshot is saved into the output directory as `page-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg|webp}`.

fullPage.description: When true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Cannot be used with element screenshots.

scale.description: Image resolution scale. "css" produces a screenshot sized in CSS pixels (smaller, consistent across devices). "device" produces a high-resolution screenshot using device pixels (larger, accounts for the device pixel ratio). Default is css.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page, this is better than screenshot

target.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

filename.description: Save snapshot to a file instead of returning it in the response. Relative file names are resolved against the workspace root.

depth.description: Limit the depth of the snapshot tree

boxes.description: Include each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height] in the snapshot. Coordinates are viewport-relative, in CSS pixels (Element.getBoundingClientRect)

tools.description: Perform click on a web page

doubleClick.description: Whether to perform a double click instead of a single click

button.description: Button to click, defaults to left

endTarget.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot, or a unique element selector

tools.description: Hover over element on page

instructions:
CORA's fixer (cora:a11y-fixer or cora-a11y-fixer in Claude Code, a11y_fixer in Codex) calls CORA's tools itself. Any other agent that can dispatch it does, in Codex with fork_turns "none", for any task needing CORA's tools, questions too. It never sees your conversation: give it the person's request verbatim, what it refers to and its scope, such as report only or no edits. Any other subagent that cannot dispatch names the files to check in its answer. Only where no fixer exists, use CORA's tools directly.

Present the fixer's summary with cora:a11y-report if you have it, without rescanning; relay other answers as they are.

CORA's automated rules find only some accessibility problems, so neither a clean scan nor a fix verify_fix found fixed shows that a page conforms to WCAG; never claim it does.

An issue is what a scan's result lists under one ID. Each opens a loop: verify_fix records each attempt in it, and summarize_fixes ends it.

When you use CORA's tools:
- Use this server's browser_* tools: CORA scans only its browser.
- scan_url loads and scans a page; scan_page scans it as it is now; list_rules lists the rules.
- For each fix, call explain_finding and get_fix_guidance, with framework for a UI framework it accepts, edit, then call verify_fix and follow its next step.
- Call verify_fix only for an issue you changed: every verdict but fixed counts as an attempt toward escalating it.
- Call summarize_fixes last, and again while its omitted is above 0. A question that needs no scan needs no summary.
- A JavaScript dialog blocks scanning: answer it with browser_handle_dialog first.

If the person wants CORA to stop asking for its fixer after UI edits, tell them to type /cora:pause in Claude Code or $cora:pause in Codex, which only they can invoke; /cora:resume or $cora:resume undoes it.
